proposals: PNGRB should publish a forecast-against-outturn review whenever it issues a long-range gas demand projection, setting earlier projections such as the 2013 report’s 746 MMSCMD for 2029–30 against actual consumption, so a new roadmap explains what the last one got wrong rather than leaving it unmentioned.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and PNGRB should publish an item-by-item action-taken statement on the Vision 2040 committee’s recommendations, marking each accepted, rejected or under consideration with a date, so readers can see which proposals, including those that drew dissent, actually moved.

PNGRB should report each year city gas entities’ progress against their submitted 2030 work plans, by geographical area, so the gap between about 14.19 million PNG connections and 7,513 CNG stations in December 2024 and the planned 120 million and 17,500 can be tracked against the CGD-led demand growth the report relies on.

PNGRB should publish annually India’s LNG storage cover in days of national gas consumption, with tanks commissioned against the 10–11 the committee estimated, so progress from about 12 days towards a 20-day buffer by FY2030 is measurable.

PNGRB should publish the input assumptions and scenario tables behind its in-house “Good to Go” and “Good to Best” demand cases, so the 297–630 MMSCMD range at the heart of the roadmap can be tested by others rather than taken as given.
